title: Dependency-Aware Circuit Scheduling for Multi-Core Quantum Systems to Minimize Makespan
authors: Rajeswari Suance P S, Ruchika Gupta, Maurizio Palesi, John Jose
abstract: Multi-core quantum computing architectures have emerged as a promising solution to the qubit scalability limitations of monolithic NISQ devices. Quantum algorithms are expressed as quantum circuits composed of single- and two-qubit gates. However, circuit scheduling in multi-core quantum systems remains largely unexplored. Reducing overall execution time (makespan), increasing core utilization, and hiding communication latency behind computation depends on effective scheduling. In this paper, we first introduce a layered scheduling approach as a baseline where quantum gates within the same layer are executed in parallel, while layers themselves are executed sequentially. We then propose a greedy scheduling strategy which schedules each gate as soon as all its dependencies and required resources are available. This allows fine-grained parallelism across cores. Our evaluation shows that on real benchmarks, greedy scheduling achieves an average 40% reduction in makespan and improvement in core utilization. The results suggest that the use of intelligent circuit scheduling to exploit parallelism can greatly enhance the speed of circuit execution in multi-core quantum architectures.
summary: This paper tackles the critical challenge of circuit scheduling on multi-core quantum processors by proposing a dependency-aware greedy algorithm. This method allows for fine-grained parallelism, significantly improving execution speed compared to simpler layer-based approaches. The results demonstrate that intelligent scheduling can drastically reduce makespan and better utilize hardware resources in these complex quantum systems.
main_problem: The core problem is developing effective circuit scheduling algorithms for multi-core quantum systems to minimize the overall execution time (makespan).
main_result: Dependency-aware greedy scheduling achieves substantial performance gains, showing an average 40% reduction in makespan compared to baseline layered scheduling on real benchmarks.
method: The authors propose a dependency-aware greedy scheduling strategy that schedules each gate at the earliest possible time based on resource and data dependencies, contrasting it with rigid layer-by-layer execution.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a multi-core quantum computing architecture utilizing an n x n 2D mesh topology. Inter-core operations rely on quantum teleportation over a Network-on-Chip (NoC).
key_observables: Makespan ($	ext{T}_{	ext{total}}$), Core Utilization, and Communication Overlap Ratio ($	ext{R}_{	ext{comm}}$).
important_parameters: The communication delay is proportional to the number of hops ($H 	imes \lambda_{	ext{hop}}$), which is a critical bottleneck.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption addressed is that fine-grained parallelism can be exploited by overlapping computation and communication latency, overcoming limitations imposed by strict layered scheduling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the multi-core architecture (NoC/Quantum Channel), compare makespans between layered vs. greedy scheduling using case studies, and show performance metrics across synthetic and real quantum circuits (QAOA, QFT).
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical model and the limitations of baseline layered scheduling. It then details the proposed dependency-aware greedy algorithm, followed by extensive evaluation on both synthetic random circuits and established real benchmarks to validate performance gains.
why_interesting: While focused on classical scheduling algorithms for quantum hardware, the analysis of communication bottlenecks (teleportation latency) and resource management in a distributed quantum setting is highly relevant to understanding physical constraints in large-scale quantum computation architectures.

Fig. 4a shows the comparative study of makespan for syn- thetic random circuits across different hardware configurations. We can see that proposed greedy scheduling algorithm con- sistently achieves a lower makespan than layered scheduling. This improvement arises because the greedy approach exploits inter-layer parallelism, allowing gates to execute as soon as their dependencies and resources are available. In contrast, the layered scheduling ignores the fine-grained parallelism and fails to hide inter-core communication latency, which is particularly evident for the larger meshes.
